title: Blake Anderson with Roy Lee: niche-by-niche wrapper marketing, short-form distribution and risk
summary: In a conversation with Cluely founder Roy Lee, Blake Anderson explains how one multi-tool AI product can be marketed separately in each niche, why UX is the real differentiator, and why short-form fragmentation and risk-taking drive outsized wins. Most of the interview is Roy's story. Blake's contributions are shorter asides on distribution and compounding.

principles.text: Bundle many single-function AI tools into one app, but market it separately to each niche, leading with only that niche's feature.
principles.quote: within the astrology niche you can say this is going to give you your AI horoscope report and you don't talk about the other features and then you're marketing the same exact company the same exact product

principles.text: In consumer AI, frontier models are roughly equal, so UX and smoothness decide who wins.
principles.quote: then the big difference is just like what's the UX? How smooth is the the actual application?

principles.text: Short-form social is fragmented into separate pockets, and builders who live outside them (like engineers) miss how valuable it is.
principles.quote: different pockets of the internet really exist more today than they ever have.

principles.text: Winning in content is streaky: many flops, then one hit unlocks a run of hits, so keep shipping and compounding.
principles.quote: It's like why is it that you can try 20 pieces of content, everyone flops, then you get one hits, and then the next 10 [ __ ] hit.

principles.text: Risk-taking is positive expected value: several small losses are outweighed by occasional big upside if you keep compounding.
principles.quote: one in every five maybe is 10 10 upside um and if you're the sort of person where you're like I'm just going to keep compounding

principles.text: Attention is the real currency online, more than credibility or reputation.
principles.quote: It seems like the real currency is uh, you know, it's just attention.
